jobs.occupation: Engineering Underwriter - Process Industries and new Technologies (m/f/d)* (Underwriter (Versicherung))
jobs.description:
Go beyond and create global impact: At Munich Re, we're proud to be one of the world's leading providers of reinsurance, primary insurance, and insurance-related risk solutions. Our group is made up of the reinsurance and ERGO business segments, along with our asset management company, MEAG. We operate globally and are active in all lines of the insurance business.
Since our founding in 1880, we've built a reputation for unrivalled risk-related expertise and a solid financial foundation. We use our strengths to support our clients' business goals and drive technological progress. We're also at the forefront of developing coverage for emerging risks, from rocket launches and renewable energy to cyber threats and artificial intelligence.
With around 44,000 people worldwide, our group's corporate culture is defined by performance, mutual respect, and trust. All this makes us an attractive employer providing global career development opportunities and prospects.
Global investment in industrial plants and infrastructure is being driven by evolving technologies, resilient supply chains, the energy transition and growing demand for critical resources. Munich Re F&C provides tailored insurance solutions for complex international construction projects, including oil, gas, chemicals and petrochemicals, mining and mineral processing, battery and semiconductor manufacturing, and emerging energy technologies such as green hydrogen, carbon capture and eSAF. As part of our Construction team, you will combine engineering expertise with commercial decision-making. We welcome applicants from insurance, industry, project development, EPC contracting and risk engineering. Prior underwriting experience is not essential if you bring relevant technical or contract expertise, sound judgement and a willingness to learn the insurance business.
Your Job

- Assess and underwrite complex international construction and industrial projects in line with Munich Re's strategy, risk appetite and delegated authority.
- Analyse technical, contractual and commercial information, identify key risk drivers and uncertainties, and document the decision process.
- Develop tailored insurance solutions that balance client needs, risk quality and sustainable profitability.
- Identify attractive business opportunities and contribute to profitable growth, portfolio quality, and diversification.
- Build trusted relationships with brokers, insureds and project stakeholders, and represent Munich Re at client meetings, project presentations and market events.
- Participate in or lead site surveys and translate findings into reports.
- Collaborate with colleagues and specialist experts, support the global Munich Re organisation and contribute to underwriting methods, tools and knowledge sharing.

Your Profile

- A university degree in engineering, natural sciences or other relevant technical disciplines, or a recognised insurance qualification with a strong interest in technical risks.
- Professional experience in process-driven industries, equipment manufacturing or another relevant technical environment, or experience in construction project insurance.
- The ability to understand complex industrial processes, project structures, and to derive clear conclusions from complex or incomplete information.
- The ability to familiarize yourself quickly with new topics, work independently, take ownership and make well-reasoned decisions.
- Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills, combined with a constructive and solution-oriented approach.
- The ability to analyse technical and contractual documents and the motivation to develop expertise in insurance contracts and policy wordings.
- Curiosity about industrial sectors and emerging technologies, combined with an international and collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively across cultures and functions.
- Fluent written and spoken English is required for working in an international business environment. German, Spanish or other relevant language skills are an advantage.
- Willingness to travel internationally.

Application Instructions
Please apply through our online portal and upload your CV, as well as your academic reference letters, including school certificates, graduation certificates and transcripts of record for any degrees. If applicable, please also submit reference letters from any previous employers or certificates from any other qualifications you may have. We recommend writing a cover letter to tell us more about why the position and Munich Re is of interest to you.
About us
As the world's leading reinsurance company with more than 16,000 employees at over 50 locations, Munich Re introduces a paradigm shift in the way you think about insurance. By turning uncertainty into a manageable risk we enable fundamental change. Join us working on topics today that will concern society tomorrow, whether that be climate change, major construction projects, medical risk assessment or even space travel.
Together we embrace a culture where multiskilled teams dare to think big. We create the new and the different for our clients and cultivate innovation.
Sounds like you? Push boundaries with us and be part of Munich Re.
Our employees are our greatest strength. That's why we offer them a wide range of benefits. You can find some examples below.
Unlock your potential

- Diversity, Equity & Inclusion: we embrace the power of differences and are convinced that diversity fosters innovation and resilience and enables us to act braver and better.
- Continuous Learning: we believe that continuous learning is a key differentiator and critical for building new skills and accelerating growth.
- Career Mobility: we actively support career mobility, and our strong global and regional presence offers a wealth of career growth opportunities for you.

Rewards & Recognition

- Competitive salary: appropriate compensation for your high level of commitment.
- Retirement provision: state of the art in-house pension solutions.
- Work-life balance: promoting the compatibility of family and work in addition to overall work-life balance.
- Health management: focus on your physical and mental health far beyond legal requirements.
- Hybrid working: living the best of both worlds - we offer you a very flexible approach as well as the opportunity to work from abroad on an occasional basis.
- Munich Re not only stands for fairness with regard to its clients; it is also an equal opportunities employer. Severely disabled candidates will also be prioritized, if equally qualified.

jobs.occupation: Working Student (d/f/m) in the area of Mass Properties (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

In order to support Mass Properties department, Airbus Defence and Space is looking for a

Working Student (d/f/m) in the area of Mass Properties

You are a full time student, looking for a working student position and want to get to know the work of a Working Student (d/f/m) in the area of Mass Properties?  Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Mass Properties department as a working student (d/f/m) with approx. 18 hours a week!

- Location: Manching
- Start: January 2027
- Duration: 12 months

Definition working student

Working students (d/f/m) are students who are enrolled at a University or some other institution of higher education, and who are employed in a reasonably long, fixed-term position parallel to their studies. This position must not be confused with an internship or with the possibility of writing a final thesis.

This employment usually takes place directly on the company's premises. A working student's main focus remains on their studies, which is why, during term-time, working students are not allowed to work more than 20 hours per week.

Working students therefore usually work near their place of study, so as to conveniently combine studying and employment.

Your location

Located about an hour’s drive north of Munich, Manching is an up-and-coming market town that offers a wide range of leisure and cultural activities. Here, you can enjoy the quality of life in the countryside while the pleasures of near-by cities are still within easy reach.

Our mission

Mass Properties Manching is responsible for defining, calculating, and controlling the mass data set throughout the entire life‑cycle of an aircraft. This data set includes mass, centre of gravity and moment of inertia at component, system and aircraft levels. It is required, for example, for the preliminary design of future projects, structural design, system development, support of flight‑test campaigns, and in‑service support. Consequently, the department maintains interfaces with a variety of disciplines, both within and outside the Flight Physics domain. To keep the growing mass properties data set organised and to trace every change throughout the development of our new projects, we are building a Python‑driven, SQLite‑backed database application. In parallel, we are exploring how AI‑based automation can further increase the efficiency and accuracy of our analyses.

Your benefits

- Attractive salary and work-life balance with an 18-hour week (flexitime).
- A final thesis is possible after consultation with the department.
- Mobile working after agreement with the department.
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Python Software Development: Develop, maintain, and improve Python-based applications and reusable software components for managing aircraft mass data.
- Database Management: Support the design and implementation of database structures, queries, and data models using relational databases.
- Workflow Automation: Identify and automate repetitive engineering workflows and data-processing tasks to increase efficiency.
- Data Integration & Processing: Develop tools for importing, validating, transforming, and integrating data from various engineering sources and tools.
- AI Research & Prototyping: Investigate and evaluate the application of AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) by developing prototypes for engineering workflows.
- Software Quality Assurance: Ensure software reliability by developing automated/manual test cases, documenting bugs, and improving code maintainability.

Desired skills and qualifications

- Enrolled full-time student (d/f/m) in Computer Science, Data Science, Informatics, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
- Good programming skills in Python and a strong interest in software development.
- Basic knowledge or a strong interest in the following areas: SQL and relational databases (e.g., SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL), Software architecture and Object-Oriented Programming, Data processing, automation, and software testing.
- Interest in learning and working with technologies such as: PyQt for GUI development, Git for version control, Jira and Confluence for project management, AI and Large Language Models (LLMs).
- Ability to translate complex engineering problems into structured software solutions through a self-organized and analytical way of working.
- Advanced English; German is a plus.

Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth.

Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!

Hungry, Humble, Honest, with Heart.

The Opportunity

Nutanix is seeking a highly strategic alliance leader and executive partner to lead, scale, and manage our overall global partnership with SAP. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Alliances and Business Development, you will be the primary global business owner and overall executive manager responsible for translating strategic imperatives into high-impact product roadmap alignment, executive alignment, market adoption, and direct revenue.

This is an executive-level partnership management role owning the end-to-end global SAP alliance. Rather than managing static partner channels, you will serve as the chief relationship owner—navigating SAP’s executive hierarchy, driving C-suite, SVP, and VP-level alignment, establishing executive sponsorship, and shaping joint go-to-market (GTM) motions. We are specifically seeking candidates with deep domain strength on at least one side of this partnership—ideally both:

- Profile A (SAP Native): A leader with deep SAP ecosystem expertise and an established network of relationships across SAP executive, GTM, and product leadership.
- Profile B (Nutanix Insider): A leader with deep Nutanix product, organizational, and GTM knowledge who possesses established ties into the SAP ecosystem.

Based in Germany, this position carries worldwide responsibility for the SAP alliance while driving secondary strategic EMEA partnerships (such as NetApp) where geographic and portfolio synergies exist. This position will require travel to SAP Headquarters as well as related business travel needs.

About the Team

The Strategic Alliances organization at Nutanix is a high-impact team focused on building and scaling partnerships that help enterprises modernize infrastructure and simplify hybrid multi-cloud operations. Our team collaborates cross-functionally with Product Management, Systems Engineering, Sales and Marketing to deliver differentiated, outcome-based solutions to our customers. What sets us apart is our dedication to building strong, enduring partnerships that solve complex business challenges and drive measurable commercial impact.

Key Responsibilities

Build & Own the Global SAP Partnership (Primary Focus)

- Serve as the global business lead and overall manager for the SAP alliance, defining long-term strategic vision, executive governance, and global growth frameworks.
- Act as the primary executive interface between Nutanix and SAP, engaging directly with C-level executives, SVPs, corporate strategy heads, product VPs, and global alliance leadership.
- Secure executive sponsorship across SAP and Nutanix leadership to prioritize joint strategic initiatives and resource allocations.
- Formulate and facilitate Executive Steering Committees, Executive Business Reviews (EBRs), and operational check-ins with executive stakeholders to govern performance against shared KPIs and OKRs.

Drive Revenue, Co-Selling, and Go-To-Market Execution

- Translate alliance strategies into high-performing commercial motions, leveraging executive-level GTM sponsorship to unlock complex target accounts.
- Lead high-level deal escalation and sponsor strategic account reviews alongside regional EMEA sales leadership and executive sponsors, building scalable engagement models for AMER and APJ.
- Structure and negotiate high-impact alliance frameworks, joint GTM models, and commercial terms in close collaboration with executive stakeholders in Legal, Finance, and Business Development.

Advance Product & Solution Alignment

- Collaborate with Nutanix Product Management, Engineering, Solutions Architecture, and Marketing to drive technical alignment with SAP.
- Advance compatibility, supportability, and certification paths (including Nutanix AHV where applicable) to remove customer adoption barriers.
- Align Nutanix enterprise infrastructure solutions with SAP’s core application and platform roadmap.

Manage Secondary Strategic Partnerships (EMEA)

- Drive business development and partner growth for strategic partnerships in EMEA (including NetApp), leveraging complementary infrastructure solutions.
- Identify cross-partner synergies to unlock joint enterprise opportunities.
- Adapt and support additional regional alliance initiatives as business priorities evolve.

What You Will Bring

Primary Experience Profiles (Must fit at least one profile, ideally both)

- Profile A (SAP Native): A leader with deep SAP ecosystem expertise and an established, active network across SAP executive leadership (SVP/VP), C-suite influencers, GTM, and product leadership.
- Profile B (Nutanix Insider): A leader with deep Nutanix product and GTM knowledge who possesses established executive credibility and relationships within the SAP ecosystem.

Qualifications & Core Competencies

- 10+ years of progressive experience in strategic alliances, partner management, or enterprise tech leadership, with at least 5 years leading global, Tier-1 executive partnerships.
- Executive Partnership Leadership: Demonstrated track record of overall management and governance of strategic multi-million-dollar tech alliances.
- Executive Presence & Influence: Superior communication and negotiation skills with a proven ability to engage, advise, and influence C-suite, SVP, and VP stakeholders across complex, matrixed global organizations.
- Proven Business Builder: Track record of mobilizing executive sponsors, driving net-new pipeline, and structuring global partnership agreements.
- Entrepreneurial Execution: High urgency, comfort with ambiguity, and a hands-on approach to building programs from scratch.
- Cross-Functional Leadership: Authentic, collaborative leader who builds trust, drives cross-functional alignment across Sales, Marketing, Product, and Legal, and operates with operational rigor.
- Languages & Location: Based in Germany. Fluent English communication skills required; professional German language proficiency preferred.
- Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree or MBA preferred.

What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months)

- Executive Governance & Alignment: Established a formal Executive Governance Charter, active C-suite/VP executive sponsorship, and a structured cadence of Executive Business Reviews (EBRs) across Nutanix and SAP leadership.

Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d)

The Semiconductor Laboratory (HLL) of the Max Planck Society, located on the research campus in Garching near Munich, is a leading facility for the development of highly precise radiation sensors and detector systems. On approximately 1,400 m² of cleanroom space, HLL develops, fabricates and tests advanced semiconductor detectors for applications in X-ray astronomy, particle physics and materials research. With around 50 employees from different nationalities, HLL provides a highly international and interdisciplinary environment in which scientists, engineers and technology specialists work closely together across the entire development chain — from fundamental research and simulation to device design, fabrication and experimental characterization.

To strengthen our activities in quantum sensing and advanced quantum-device technologies, and to provide scientific and technological support to our research, engineering and service teams, we are looking for a Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d) to join our team at the earliest possible date on a full-time basis (39 hours/week). 

Your responsibilities

- Develop and optimize quantum sensor concepts based on qubit systems and quantum effects.
- Perform advanced numerical simulations and modeling of qubit-based sensing systems, including relevant physical processes, noise sources and system-level performance.
- Work closely with technology development, engineering and experimental teams to translate simulation results into practical implementations.
- Analyze experimental data and use the results to refine physical models and sensor designs.
- Contribute to scientific publications, technical documentation and intellectual property.

Your profile

- PhD in physics, electrical engineering, applied physics, quantum engineering or a related field.
- Background in quantum sensing, qubit control and precision measurement.
- Experience with numerical simulation, modeling and system design.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills combined with a practical, technology-oriented mindset.
- Strong motivation to work in close cooperation with technology, engineering and experimental teams.
- Fluency in English; knowledge of German is an advantage.

Advantageous experience

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be particularly valuable:

- Cleanroom / semiconductor / microfabrication experience
- Familiarity with Python, MATLAB, COMSOL or equivalent 
- MEMS/NEMS or integrated sensor technologies
- Precision measurement and low-noise instrumentation
- Experience bridging qubit physics, device design and fabrication technology

What we offer

- International environment, diverse responsibilities and a high degree of autonomy: Flat hierarchies and a collaborative, agile team within an internationally renowned research institution. You will work closely with scientists, engineers and technology specialists across disciplines and have the opportunity to shape the development of innovative quantum-sensing technologies.
- Advantages of the public sector: Remuneration according to the German public service pay scale TVöD (Bund), depending on qualifications and experience; occupational pension scheme (VBL); 30 days of annual leave (31 days as of 2027), plus additional days off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve. The position is initially limited to two years, with the possibility of subsequent permanent employment.
- Work-life balance and compatibility of family and career: Flexible working hours (flextime), opportunities for mobile working, support in finding childcare and care for family members, and a comprehensive company health management program.
- Professional development: Thorough onboarding and opportunities for internal and external training and further education tailored to your individual needs. You will have the opportunity to continuously develop your expertise in quantum sensing, qubit technology, simulation and semiconductor technology.
- Research campus: Excellent access by public transport, including the possibility of a monthly subsidy for the “Deutschland-Job-Ticket”, or by car with free parking in the immediate vicinity of the laboratory. A canteen and further dining options are available nearby, as well as campus-wide events and activities.

The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. The Max Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society seeks to increase the number of women in those areas where they are underrepresented and therefore explicitly encourages women to apply.

Further information and application

Detailed information about the Semiconductor Laboratory (HLL) can be found at HLL – Semiconductor Laboratory (http://www.hll.mpg.de/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) .

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Jelena Ninkovic, Tel.: +49 89 839400-49.

Include the names of three referees that can be contacted in your CV.

We look forward to receiving your application!

jobs.occupation: Credit Analyst for Financial Institutions and Non-Bank Financial Institutions (m/f/d)* (Underwriter (Versicherung))
jobs.description:
Go beyond and create global impact: At Munich Re, we're proud to be one of the world's leading providers of reinsurance, primary insurance, and insurance-related risk solutions. Our group is made up of the reinsurance and ERGO business segments, along with our asset management company, MEAG. We operate globally and are active in all lines of the insurance business.
Since our founding in 1880, we've built a reputation for unrivalled risk-related expertise and a solid financial foundation. We use our strengths to support our clients' business goals and drive technological progress. We're also at the forefront of developing coverage for emerging risks, from rocket launches and renewable energy to cyber threats and artificial intelligence.
With around 44,000 people worldwide, our group's corporate culture is defined by performance, mutual respect, and trust. All this makes us an attractive employer providing global career development opportunities and prospects.
Munich Re is writing business mainly with global banks by insuring credit risks originated by the banks - either on single risk basis (Global Credit Solutions - GCS) or on the basis of structured portfolio transactions (Structured Portfolio Solutions - SPS). Your role as Credit Analyst (Risk Underwriter) is to support the teams by conducting risk analyses of financial institutions and sovereigns, from emerging markets in particular, as well as assessing complex financing transactions in the field of export trade finance, and making the necessary preparations for independent credit decisions in conjunction with the Client Relationship & Risk Manager (CRRM).
Your Job

- Analysis of creditworthiness of banks and non-bank financial institutions as well as evaluation of complex financing structures in the field of trade finance
- Determination of maximum risk appetite for individual banks and banking sectors on country-level
- Assessment of country risks in the context of financing transactions of sovereigns
- Prepare internal credit applications, making informed recommendations and providing internal stakeholders and clients with reasoned explanations for decisions
- Monitoring and steering the existing financial institutions portfolio with a global scope; identification of significant risks at an early stage and initiating appropriate risk measures
- Developing and enhancing existing tools and credit risk management systems
- Cooperate closely with a deal team as well as involvement in direct client contacts
- Participate in regular client meetings to discuss transactions, portfolio developments and relevant market and credit developments.
- Take initiative with regard to the examination and development of strategic growth initiatives and new business opportunities
- Support efforts to enhance existing tools, credit risk management systems and processes

Your Profile

- University / Master degree, preferably in business or economics or with a scientific focus; additional qualifications such as CFA or equivalent are a strong advantage
- At least 7 years' professional experience in the credit analysis of banks and non-bank financial institutions (preferably in emerging markets)
- Relevant product knowledge in trade finance and general financing transactions of banks and NBFIs
- Good knowledge of sovereign risk analysis
- In-depth knowledge of credit risk management in banks, including development finance/multilateral institutions, and keen interest in economic, political, and regulatory topics
- Excellent analytical skills combined with a pronounced risk awareness and sense of responsibility, independent and result-oriented working style, ability to justify decisions in a clear and comprehensible manner
- Proficient use of MS-Office (especially Excel and Power BI) and interest in AI supported analysis
- Strong team player and confident demeanour, able to contribute in a dynamic and collaborative environment
- Very good written and verbal command of English; additional business-relevant language skills are an advantage

Application Instructions
Please apply through our online portal and upload your CV, as well as your academic reference letters, including school certificates, graduation certificates and transcripts of record for any degrees. If applicable, please also submit reference letters from any previous employers or certificates from any other qualifications you may have. We recommend writing a cover letter to tell us more about why the position and Munich Re is of interest to you.
About us
As the world's leading reinsurance company with more than 16,000 employees at over 50 locations, Munich Re introduces a paradigm shift in the way you think about insurance. By turning uncertainty into a manageable risk we enable fundamental change. Join us working on topics today that will concern society tomorrow, whether that be climate change, major construction projects, medical risk assessment or even space travel.
Together we embrace a culture where multiskilled teams dare to think big. We create the new and the different for our clients and cultivate innovation.
Sounds like you? Push boundaries with us and be part of Munich Re.
Our employees are our greatest strength. That's why we offer them a wide range of benefits. You can find some examples below.
Unlock your potential

- Diversity, Equity & Inclusion: we embrace the power of differences and are convinced that diversity fosters innovation and resilience and enables us to act braver and better.
- Continuous Learning: we believe that continuous learning is a key differentiator and critical for building new skills and accelerating growth.
- Career Mobility: we actively support career mobility, and our strong global and regional presence offers a wealth of career growth opportunities for you.

Rewards & Recognition

- Competitive salary: appropriate compensation for your high level of commitment.
- Retirement provision: state of the art in-house pension solutions.
- Work-life balance: promoting the compatibility of family and work in addition to overall work-life balance.
- Health management: focus on your physical and mental health far beyond legal requirements.
- Hybrid working: living the best of both worlds - we offer you a very flexible approach as well as the opportunity to work from abroad on an occasional basis.
- Munich Re not only stands for fairness with regard to its clients; it is also an equal opportunities employer. Severely disabled candidates will also be prioritized, if equally qualified.
